summary: Sporting News live blog of Game 4 of the 2023 World Series at Chase Field, where the Texas Rangers beat the Arizona Diamondbacks 11-7 to take a 3-1 series lead. Texas scored five runs in each of the second and third innings for a 10-0 lead, led by Marcus Semien and Corey Seager, and Arizona rallied late but fell short. The Rangers now need one more win for their first championship, with Nathan Eovaldi starting Game 5 against Zac Gallen.
one_line: The Rangers beat the Diamondbacks 11-7 in World Series Game 4 after a 10-run second and third inning, moving one win from their first title.
key_facts: The Rangers beat the Diamondbacks 11-7 in Game 4 on Tuesday, Oct. 31, 2023 at Chase Field in Phoenix, taking a 3-1 World Series lead.
Texas scored five runs in the second inning and five in the third to build a 10-0 lead over Arizona's bullpen.
Marcus Semien drove in five of the Rangers' first 10 runs, including a 2-run triple and a 3-run home run that made it 10-0.
Corey Seager hit a 2-run home run off Kyle Nelson, his third home run of the series; all three of his hits in the series are homers, but he is hitting under .200.
Adolis Garcia's season ended with a moderate oblique strain; Ezequiel Duran was added to the roster and Travis Jankowski took his place in the lineup.
Max Scherzer was also taken off the Rangers' World Series roster and replaced by Brock Burke.
Arizona scored six runs over the final two innings, including a 3-run home run by Lourdes Gurriel Jr. in the eighth and a 2-run single by Gabriel Moreno in the ninth.
Jonah Heim homered to right field in the eighth to restore Texas' 10-run lead, and Josh Jung had a three-hit night.
Bruce Bochy brought in closer Jose Leclerc for the final out despite a six-run lead; Walker popped out in foul territory to end the game.
Ketel Marte extended his postseason hitting streak to 20 games with a leadoff single in the first inning.
Nathan Eovaldi will make his sixth start of the postseason for Texas in Game 5, and Zac Gallen will start for Arizona, which faces elimination for the third time this postseason.
Emmanuel Rivera replaced Evan Longoria in the Diamondbacks' Game 4 lineup.
Fox carried the series, with Joe Davis on play-by-play and John Smoltz as analyst.
